subject: AegisBank - confirmation of log review and no-exfiltration summary
messages:
From: Anna Kim <anna.kim@aegisbank.com>

Cc: AegisBank Security <security@aegisbank.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T09:12:00Z
Subject: Observed anomaly and request for integrity confirmation

Hi Rohan,

Thanks for the quick standby on this. Our monitoring flagged a small volume of anomalous GET requests to your inference endpoint between 2026-09-11T23:54:00Z and 2026-09-12T00:08:00Z. We don't have evidence of data exfiltration on our side yet, but compliance wants a vendor-side affirmation that no customer payloads were leaked or exported.

Can you confirm whether Redwood's logs show any unusually large outbound transfers or any access that would indicate data export? If possible, please provide a short summary of the log verification steps and a hash summary for the relevant log slices. Our audit team will need something we can archive.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Anna
Anna Kim
Head, Third-Party Risk
AegisBank

Hi Anna — thank you for the heads-up and for the timeframe. We're on it.

Planned immediate actions:
- Triage and isolate the request window (2026-09-11T23:54:00Z - 2026-09-12T00:08:00Z).
- Run a log hash reconciliation for the affected front-end and gateway slices.
- Sample token/response flows tied to the call IDs you provided (if available).
- Provide a short attestation that there is no evidence of data export from our platform, or detail any findings if we discover something.

Looping in Monica (security ops) and Jordan (support) to lead the forensic review. We expect an initial summary within 2–4 hours and a formal attestation by EOD.

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Kim <anna.kim@aegisbank.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12T11:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed anomaly and request for integrity confirmation — forensic summary attached

Hi Anna / team — Monica from Security Ops here. Quick summary of our findings after the log sweep and sampling for the specified window: 

What we checked
- Ingest gateway logs (region: us-east-1) for inbound request sizes and IP egress patterns.
- Inference runtime logs including KV cache access patterns and streaming chunk outputs.
- Network egress counters for GPUs and node agents for the time window.
- Hash reconciliation: computed SHA256 hashes for the canonical log slices and compared to immutable archival snapshots.
- Sampling of full request/response traces for 12 calls that matched the anomaly signature.

Findings (high level)
- No unusually large outbound data transfers observed at the infra or node-agent level during the window. Egress bytes are consistent with normal generation traffic.
- Hash reconciliation: all canonical slices match the archived snapshots (see attached aegis_log-hash-summary.csv).
- Sampled traces show normal token output patterns; we observed no additional extraneous payloads or exported artifacts.
- No privileged admin API usage occurred during the window; control-plane audit logs show standard maintenance activity unrelated to customer data.

Attachments included:
- aegis_log-hash-summary.csv (hashes and slice ids)
- forensic-checklist.pdf (actions performed, timestamps, and analyst notes)

Conclusion
Based on the above checks and the sampled traces, we find no evidence of data exfiltration or unauthorized exports tied to the timeframe you provided. We're preparing a short attestation you can archive; please let us know if you need a signed/formal statement on company letterhead or a more detailed packet for your auditors.

Next steps
- Rohan will send an attestation file and an internal ticket link for your records.
- If you want expanded sampling (more traces or longer retention snapshots) we can provide that on request.

Monica Patel
Security Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks again for your patience. Per Monica's analysis above, attached is a short attestation text file and the CSV hash summary for archival. Key points in the attestation: 

- We conducted a targeted forensic sweep for the window 2026-09-11T23:54:00Z - 2026-09-12T00:08:00Z across gateway, runtime, and node-agent logs.
- All reconciled canonical log slices match archived snapshots (SHA256), and sampled request/response traces show normal content generation patterns.
- No indicators of data export, exfiltration, or abnormal egress were found.

Attachments: attestation-aegis-20260912.txt, aegis_log-hash-summary.csv, forensic-checklist.pdf

For your records we've also opened internal ticket SUP-2193 (see link). If you need a signed, notarized attestation or a packaged evidence bundle for your audit, we can route that request through Legal and Compliance — let me know the preferred recipient and deadline.
